text:
anya: quick ping  I flipped tessera-int6 into a 10% staging canary and the short-query (<=12 tokens) English/ES cohort shows a Recall@1 drop vs atlas-v3. tiny sample but consistent on dashboard. anyone else? :thinking:

ops-bot: deploy complete  tessera-int6 -> staging (canary 10%). link: https://console.redwood.ai/staging/models/tessera/variants/int6

liam: re-ran the micro-holdout locally against the canary. command:
```bash
python -m eval.recall --model tessera-int6 --queries holdout/short_k1_en_es.json --k 1 --seed 7
```
result snippet:
```text
Recall@1: 0.66
Baseline (atlas-v3): 0.73
```

mei: per-lang breakdown from my run (N=1k each):
```text
lang  atlas  tessera-int6  delta
en    0.74   0.66          -0.08
es    0.72   0.63          -0.09
```

liam: ran embedding cosine diffs between atlas and tessera-int6 on anchors. mean cosine drop ~0.03 overall but for short EN/ES tails it's ~0.10. seems quant pushing these vectors off the anchor cluster.

anya: does an int8 per-channel (int8_pc) variant exist for tessera?

devex-bot: yes  tessera-int8_pc built and available in staging but not routed. you can add variant traffic without redeploy:
```bash
redwood model set-variant --model tessera --variant int8_pc --traffic 5 --env staging
```

liam: toggled int8_pc -> 5% traffic and re-ran the same eval on that slice. quick numbers:
```text
Recall@1 (int8_pc slice): 0.71
Baseline (atlas-v3): 0.73
delta: -0.02
```

mei: good recovery. also checked churn@1 between atlas and int8_pc: 0.05 vs 0.12 for int6. p95 latency impact on staging negligible (+3ms).

anya: proposed interim plan:
- route short <=12 tokens to int8_pc in staging at 25% for 24h canary
- keep int6 for long queries (>64 tokens) to preserve cost
- run 10k stratified short eval overnight (EN/ES/JA) with churn, cosine-diff, and id-flip metrics
- add alert: per-lang recall@1 drop > 0.03 absolute

liam: running overnight batch now. will upload artifacts (nn lists, cosine hist, UMAP PNGs) to RED-3622 when done.

mei: adding synthetic-suffix stress test to the eval (mutate last token and re-run) to check brittle subword behavior.

anya: great. scheduling 15m sync 09:30 PT tomorrow to review results. tagging @sre for monitoring knobs if we need to ramp traffic quickly. :thumbsup:
